subject: Reranking/Embeddings eval follow-up - retrieval latency & recall@k
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-15T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Reranking/Embeddings eval follow-up - retrieval latency & recall@k

Hi Sam, Kate - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goal: improve on-site search relevance for product search (ranking downstream of retrieval). Key metrics: recall@10 (for recall-oriented queries), retrieval latency p95/p99, and overall rerank latency end-to-end.
- Current stack: 128-d embeddings, ANN index on your infra; recall@10 ~78% on our sample queries; spikes in p99 retrieval latency up to ~350ms during peak.
- Target: recall@10 >= 90 for core queries and p95 retrieval latency < 100ms, p99 ideally < 200ms.

Proposed evaluation plan (3 tests):
1) Baseline repro: run your current pipeline over the shared 5k holdout (we'll compare metrics).
2) Embedding dim sweep: 128 vs 512 dims (same encoder) + HNSW tuning (efConstruction / efSearch). Measure recall@k (k=1,5,10), retrieval latency distrib, and memory index size.
3) Rerank + retrieval combined: candidate set size 100, reranker on top (reranker latency + end-to-end TPS).

Deliverables we'll provide / deliverables from your side:
- Redwood: we will run the three tests above in our dedicated eval environment and share the CSV of results + reproducible instructions. Attached: repro_instructions_20260215.md and a first-pass results CSV (acme_rerank_eval_20260218.csv).
- Acme: confirm the evaluation queries (we used the 5k holdout you shared) and let us know if you want to run the same experiments on your infra for apples-to-apples cost numbers.

Proposed timeline: we can run the first two tests in 48-72 hours after you confirm the dataset and index parameters. After that we can schedule a short sync to go through numbers and next steps.

Open questions:
- Do you want embeddings generated by Redwood models or do you want us to use your in-house encoder for the dim-sweep?
- Any constraints on index memory / hardware we should target for the benchmark (GPU vs CPU)?

Next steps: Sam - can you confirm the dataset and whether we should benchmark on your infra as well? Kate - can we sync on schedule for a quick readout next week?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A couple clarifications before you run the tests:

1) Cost: can you give ballpark cost comparisons vs hyperscalers (Bedrock/Vertex) for the 512-d run and for reranking at scale? We need to show this to our infra team.
2) Latency expectations: you noted p95 <100ms; do you have p99 numbers from prior customers when running 512-d vectors with HNSW? Our spikes are painful for UX.
3) For the dim sweep, please keep vector quantization off for the first pass so we see raw recall differences.

If you can include the above in the results CSV, that would be ideal. We'll confirm the dataset (the 5k holdout is good) and the infra-run ask by EOD.

Hi Sam - quick technical notes to answer your questions before Marissa kicks off the runs:

- p99 numbers (512-d, HNSW on typical infra): in our prior benchmarks for ecommerce-style catalogs, we've seen p95 ~ 60-90ms and p99 ~ 120-220ms when running on modest CPU nodes with tuned efSearch. GPU ANN solutions can push p99 lower (~80-140ms) but add cost for embedding generation/serving. These ranges depend on efSearch, M (HNSW) and index size.
- Cost comparison (very rough ballparks for you to share with infra team): for a steady-state 512-d retrieval + rerank flow (100 qps candidate set 100, reranker on a small GPU):
  - Hyperscaler managed endpoints (per-request managed embedding + ANN): estimated ~2.5-4x the per-token/embedding compute cost vs Redwood Dedicated, primarily due to endpoint overhead and less batching optimization.
  - Redwood Dedicated/private eval: we optimize batching and KV cache; ballpark 0.6-1.5x the cost of hyperscaler (depends on reserved capacity and quantization).
- Quantization: agree with Sam - keep quantization off for the first pass. We'll run a second pass with 8-bit quantized embeddings to show memory/cost tradeoffs.
- Repro instructions: the attached repro_instructions_20260215.md has exact efConstruction/efSearch values we used; we recommend efSearch=200 for the 512-d run as a starting point.

I'll include p95/p99 columns and a high-level cost delta column in the CSV. We'll also include index memory and end-to-end rerank latency.

Aditya
